strings.b-00-meta.title: Describing Motion Around Us
strings.b-00-meta.objectives.0: After this lesson you can describe position, distance and displacement of an object moving in a straight line.
strings.b-00-meta.objectives.1: After this lesson you can calculate average speed, average velocity and average acceleration and use graphs to find them.
strings.b-00-meta.objectives.2: After this lesson you can use the kinematic equations for constant acceleration and explain uniform circular motion.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.0.definition: Net change in position between two instants, with magnitude and direction.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.1.definition: Displacement divided by the time interval.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.2.definition: Change in velocity divided by the time interval.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.3.definition: Steepness of a graph line, giving a rate of change.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.4.definition: Motion in a circle at constant speed with changing velocity direction.
strings.b-00-meta.glossary.5.definition: A line touching a circle at only one point.
strings.b-01.paragraphs.0: Everything around us is in motion, from butterflies and horses to clouds and tides. To study this variety simply, scientists first study idealised forms such as linear motion.
strings.b-01.paragraphs.1: Linear motion is motion in a straight line. It is the simplest kind of motion. Examples are a ball falling vertically, a car on a straight highway and a train on a straight track.
strings.b-02.caption: Reference point O and positions B and A on a straight line. Right of O is positive.
strings.b-03.paragraphs.0: To describe position we first fix a reference point. The distance and direction from that point at any instant describe the position.
strings.b-03.paragraphs.1: If position changes with time, the object is in motion. If position does not change with time, the object is at rest. On a straight line, right of O is positive and left of O is negative.
strings.b-04.question: An object is said to be in motion when its position with respect to the reference point changes with time. What does this mean for a truck ahead of you?
strings.b-04.options.0: It is at rest if it is far away
strings.b-04.options.1: It is in motion if its position changes with time
strings.b-04.options.2: It is in motion only if it is fast
strings.b-04.options.3: Distance alone is enough to describe position
strings.b-04.explanation: Motion is judged by change of position with respect to a reference point, not by speed alone. Distance and direction together describe position.
strings.b-05.paragraphs.0: An athlete starts at O, reaches B, then A, then runs back to B. Total distance travelled is OA + AB = 100 m + 60 m = 160 m.
strings.b-05.paragraphs.1: Displacement between start and stop is OB = 40 m in the positive direction. Total distance and magnitude of displacement are not equal when the object turns back.
strings.b-05.paragraphs.2: Displacement needs direction and magnitude. Total distance needs only a number. Both have SI unit metre.
strings.b-06.question: A ball is thrown vertically upwards from O, moves to B and falls back to O. Which statement about displacement is true?
strings.b-06.options.1: Its magnitude can be greater than total distance travelled
strings.b-06.options.2: Its magnitude is less than or equal to total distance travelled
strings.b-06.options.3: Its magnitude is less than total distance travelled in all cases
strings.b-06.explanation: When the ball returns to O displacement is zero while total distance is not zero. Magnitude of displacement can never exceed total distance, and it equals total distance only when moving in one direction.
strings.b-07.paragraphs.0: Average speed is total distance travelled divided by the time interval. It tells how fast an object moves and has no direction.
strings.b-07.paragraphs.1: Equal distances in equal intervals means uniform motion at constant speed. Unequal distances mean non-uniform motion with increasing or decreasing speed.
strings.b-08.problem: Two postmen start walking towards each other from a distance of 210 yojanas. One travels 9 yojanas per day and the other covers 5 yojanas per day. In how many days will they meet?
strings.b-08.steps.0.title: Distance covered together in one day
strings.b-08.steps.1.title: Time to cover 210 yojanas
strings.b-08.steps.2.title: Check distances
strings.b-08.steps.2.detail: First postman 9 x 15 = 135 yojanas. Second postman 5 x 15 = 75 yojanas. Total 210 yojanas.
strings.b-09.paragraphs.0: Average velocity is displacement divided by the time interval. It is written as v_av = s/t.
strings.b-09.paragraphs.1: Its direction is the same as displacement and is shown by plus or minus sign. Its SI unit is m s-1, also measured in km h-1. It is the average rate of change of position with time.
strings.b-10.problem: Sarang takes 50 seconds to swim from one end to the other end and back in a swimming pool. Find his average speed and average velocity in 50 s.
strings.b-10.steps.0.title: Total distance
strings.b-10.steps.1.title: Displacement
strings.b-10.steps.1.detail: He returns to the start, so displacement = 0 m.
strings.b-10.steps.2.title: Average speed
strings.b-10.steps.3.title: Average velocity
strings.b-10.answer: Average speed 1 m s-1, average velocity 0 m s-1.
strings.b-11.question: You drive 200 km north in three hours, then 200 km south in two hours. What is the average speed for the entire trip?
strings.b-11.explanation: Total distance = 400 km. Total time = 5 h. Average speed = 400 / 5 = 80 km h-1. Displacement is zero, so average velocity is zero.
strings.b-12.paragraphs.0: Average acceleration is change in velocity divided by the time interval. It is (v - u) / (t2 - t1) with SI unit m s-2.
strings.b-12.paragraphs.1: If magnitude of velocity increases, acceleration is in the direction of velocity. If magnitude decreases, acceleration is opposite to velocity.
strings.b-12.paragraphs.2: Acceleration can come from change in magnitude, change in direction, or both.
strings.b-13.problem: A bus moves with velocity 36 km h-1. The driver presses the accelerator for 10 s and velocity increases to 54 km h-1. Then the bus stops in 5 s when brakes are pressed. Find average acceleration in both intervals.
strings.b-13.steps.0.title: Convert velocities
strings.b-13.steps.1.title: Accelerator interval
strings.b-13.steps.1.detail: a = (15 - 10) / 10 = 0.5 m s-2 in the direction of velocity.
strings.b-13.steps.2.title: Brake interval
strings.b-13.steps.2.detail: a = (0 - 15) / 5 = -3 m s-2. Minus sign means opposite to velocity.
strings.b-13.answer: (i) 0.5 m s-2 in direction of velocity. (ii) -3 m s-2 opposite to velocity.
strings.b-14.problem: An object dropped from a height has velocities 0 m s-1 at 0 s, 9.8 m s-1 at 1 s, 19.6 m s-1 at 2 s, 29.4 m s-1 at 3 s and 39.2 m s-1 at 4 s. Find average acceleration in each 1 s interval.
strings.b-14.steps.0.title: 0 s to 1 s
strings.b-14.steps.1.title: 1 s to 2 s, 2 s to 3 s, 3 s to 4 s
strings.b-14.steps.2.title: Conclusion
strings.b-14.steps.2.detail: Acceleration is constant at 9.8 m s-2 in the direction of motion. This is g, acceleration due to gravity.
strings.b-14.answer: Constant average acceleration 9.8 m s-2 in direction of motion.
strings.b-15.question: A scooter speedometer reading is constant. Can the scooter still be accelerating?
strings.b-15.options.0: No, constant speed means no acceleration
strings.b-15.options.1: Yes, if direction of velocity changes
strings.b-15.options.2: Yes, if it is moving fast
strings.b-15.options.3: No, acceleration needs a change in speed only
strings.b-15.explanation: Acceleration occurs when velocity changes in magnitude or direction or both. In circular motion speed is constant but direction changes, so acceleration is non-zero.
strings.b-16.paragraphs.0: Graphs show how position, velocity or acceleration changes with time. They help compare motions and find quantities.
strings.b-16.paragraphs.1: To plot, draw X and Y axes from origin O, choose time on X-axis and position on Y-axis, choose a suitable scale, mark points and join them.
strings.b-17.title: Plotting a position-time graph
strings.b-17.steps.0.title: Draw axes
strings.b-17.steps.0.detail: Draw perpendicular lines OX and OY meeting at origin O on graph paper.
strings.b-17.steps.1.title: Choose scale
strings.b-17.steps.1.detail: For Table 4.3 use X-axis 5 divisions = 1 s and Y-axis 5 divisions = 20 m.
strings.b-17.steps.2.title: Mark points
strings.b-17.steps.2.detail: At 0 s position 0 m is origin. At 1 s position 20 m, at 2 s 40 m, and so on up to 6 s 120 m.
strings.b-17.steps.3.title: Join points
strings.b-17.steps.3.detail: Joining the points gives a straight line for constant velocity data.
strings.b-18.problem: For a vehicle starting from rest and speeding up, positions are 0 m at 0 s, 1 m at 2 s, 4 m at 4 s, 9 m at 6 s, 16 m at 8 s, 25 m at 10 s and 36 m at 12 s. Plot the position-time graph.
strings.b-18.steps.0.title: Choose scale
strings.b-18.steps.0.detail: X-axis 5 divisions = 2 s, Y-axis 5 divisions = 5 m.
strings.b-18.steps.1.title: Mark points
strings.b-18.steps.1.detail: Mark each time-position pair from the table.
strings.b-18.steps.2.title: Join points
strings.b-18.steps.2.detail: Points do not fall on a straight line. Join by a curve.
strings.b-18.answer: The graph is a curve, showing velocity is increasing.
strings.b-19.title: Position-time graph and velocity
strings.b-19.description: A position-time graph is drawn from the equation position = velocity x time for constant velocity. Changing the velocity changes the steepness of the line.
strings.b-19.controls.velocity.label: Velocity (m/s)
strings.b-20.paragraphs.0: A straight line position-time graph means constant velocity. A curved graph means velocity is not constant.
strings.b-20.paragraphs.1: A line parallel to the time axis means position is not changing, so the object is at rest. A steeper line means higher velocity.
strings.b-21.problem: A position-time graph shows a vehicle at 40 m from the origin and position not changing with time. What does it indicate?
strings.b-21.steps.0.title: Read position
strings.b-21.steps.0.detail: Position stays at 40 m for all times.
strings.b-21.steps.1.title: Interpret line
strings.b-21.steps.1.detail: Line is parallel to time axis.
strings.b-21.answer: The vehicle is at rest at 40 m from the origin.
strings.b-22.problem: Position-time graphs of two objects A and B are given. Which object has higher magnitude of average velocity?
strings.b-22.steps.0.title: Compare displacement in same time
strings.b-22.steps.0.detail: Draw lines parallel to axes for the same time interval.
strings.b-22.steps.1.title: Compare slopes
strings.b-22.steps.1.detail: Displacement of B is more than A in the same time, so slope of B is steeper.
strings.b-22.answer: Velocity of B is higher than velocity of A.
strings.b-23.title: Velocity from position-time slope
strings.b-23.steps.0.title: Take part AB of graph
strings.b-23.steps.0.detail: Draw lines parallel to axes from A and B to form triangle ABC.
strings.b-23.steps.1.title: Identify sides
strings.b-23.steps.1.detail: BC is change in position s2 - s1. CA is change in time t2 - t1.
strings.b-23.steps.2.title: Divide
strings.b-23.steps.2.detail: Velocity = BC / CA = (s2 - s1)/(t2 - t1). Example (80 - 40)/(4 - 2) = 20 m s-1.
strings.b-24.paragraphs.0: A velocity-time graph shows change in velocity with time. Constant velocity gives a line parallel to X-axis and zero acceleration.
strings.b-24.paragraphs.1: Increasing velocity with a straight line gives constant acceleration in the direction of velocity. Decreasing velocity gives constant acceleration opposite to velocity.
strings.b-25.title: Velocity-time graph slope and area
strings.b-25.description: A velocity-time graph is computed from initial velocity and constant acceleration. Slope gives acceleration and area under the line gives displacement.
strings.b-25.controls.initial_velocity.label: Initial velocity (m/s)
strings.b-25.controls.acceleration.label: Acceleration (m/s2)
strings.b-26.title: Slope and area from velocity-time graph
strings.b-26.steps.0.title: Slope for acceleration
strings.b-26.steps.0.detail: Acceleration = change in velocity / change in time. Between 10 s and 20 s, (10 - 5)/10 = 0.5 m s-2. For decreasing graph it is -0.5 m s-2.
strings.b-26.steps.1.title: Area for displacement, constant velocity
strings.b-26.steps.1.detail: Area of rectangle = velocity x time. 20 m s-1 x 6 s = 120 m.
strings.b-26.steps.2.title: Area for displacement, changing velocity
strings.b-26.steps.2.detail: Between 10 s and 20 s area = rectangle + triangle = 50 m + 25 m = 75 m.
strings.b-27.paragraphs.0: Kinematic equations describe motion with constant acceleration. Acceleration at each instant equals average acceleration.
strings.b-27.paragraphs.1: The five quantities are displacement s, time t, initial velocity u, final velocity v and acceleration a. Choose the equation that fits the known quantities.
strings.b-28.title: Deriving kinematic equations
strings.b-28.steps.0.title: Velocity equation
strings.b-28.steps.0.detail: From a = (v - u)/t we get at = v - u, so v = u + at.
strings.b-28.steps.1.title: Displacement equation
strings.b-28.steps.1.detail: Displacement is area under velocity-time graph: rectangle + triangle gives s = ut + 1/2 at^2.
strings.b-28.steps.2.title: Velocity squared equation
strings.b-28.steps.2.detail: Eliminate t between the two equations to get v^2 = u^2 + 2as.
strings.b-29.problem: A car brakes with acceleration -4 m s-2. How much distance before stopping if it was moving at (i) 54 km h-1 and (ii) 108 km h-1?
strings.b-29.steps.0.title: Convert velocities
strings.b-29.steps.0.detail: (i) 54 km h-1 = 15 m s-1. (ii) 108 km h-1 = 30 m s-1. Final velocity v = 0.
strings.b-29.steps.1.title: Use v^2 = u^2 + 2as
strings.b-29.steps.2.title: Calculate
strings.b-29.answer: (i) 28.1 m (ii) 112.5 m. Higher initial speed needs much larger stopping distance.
strings.b-30.question: Which pair are the remaining two kinematic equations derived from v = u + at and s = ut + 1/2 at^2?
strings.b-30.options.0: s = vt - 1/2 at^2 and s = (u + v)/2 t
strings.b-30.options.1: v = u - at and s = ut - at^2
strings.b-30.options.2: s = vt + 1/2 at^2 and v^2 = u^2 - 2as
strings.b-30.options.3: a = (u - v)/t and s = (u - v) t
strings.b-30.explanation: The second equation comes from area of a trapezium under the velocity-time graph, giving s = (u + v)/2 t. The first follows by substitution.
strings.b-31.paragraphs.0: Motion in a plane is motion in two dimensions. Examples are a kicked ball, a satellite and a vehicle overtaking another.
strings.b-31.paragraphs.1: Uniform circular motion is motion in a circular path with constant speed. One revolution distance is the circumference, displacement is zero, average speed is 2 pi R / T and average velocity is zero.
strings.b-32.caption: Circular path A to B to C. Velocity at B is along the tangent in the direction of motion.
strings.b-33.title: Uniform circular motion
strings.b-33.description: A point moves on a circle at constant speed. Its velocity arrow is always along the tangent and changes direction continuously.
strings.b-33.controls.radius.label: Radius (m)
strings.b-33.controls.period.label: Time for one revolution (s)
strings.b-34.paragraphs.0: Velocity at a point is along the tangent to the circle in the direction of motion. A tangent meets the circle at only one point.
strings.b-34.paragraphs.1: When a marble moving inside a ring is released, it moves in a straight line in the direction at the instant of release.
strings.b-34.paragraphs.2: Uniform circular motion is an idealised model. It is useful for planets around the Sun and vehicles making circular turns.
strings.b-35.question: A man goes from home to a shop 250 m away, returns home, goes to the shop again and returns home. What are total distance and displacement from home?
strings.b-35.explanation: Four journeys of 250 m give total distance 1000 m. He ends at home, so net change in position is zero.
strings.b-36.question: A car starts from rest and its velocity reaches 24 m s-1 in 6 s. Find average acceleration and distance travelled in 6 s.
strings.b-37.question: A motorbike moving with initial velocity 28 m s-1 and constant acceleration stops after travelling 98 m. Find acceleration and time to stop.
strings.b-38.question: A truck at 54 km h-1 slows to 36 km h-1 in 36 s with constant acceleration. What distance does it travel?
strings.b-38.explanation: Convert to 15 m s-1 and 10 m s-1. Average velocity = 12.5 m s-1. Distance = 12.5 x 36 = 450 m.
strings.b-39.question: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 20 m s-1 in 5 s, travels at 20 m s-1 for 10 s, then brakes uniformly to stop in 6 s. Find total distance.
strings.b-39.explanation: Phase 1: a = 4 m s-2, s = 50 m. Phase 2: s = 200 m. Phase 3: a = -3.33 m s-2, s = 60 m. Total = 310 m.
strings.b-40.question: On a velocity-time graph, what does the area between the graph and the time axis represent?
strings.b-40.explanation: Area = velocity x time for constant velocity and area of the shape for changing velocity. Both give displacement in that time interval.
strings.b-41.question: The Earth moves around the Sun. Can an object kept on the Earth be considered at rest?
strings.b-41.options.0: No, nothing on Earth can ever be at rest
strings.b-41.options.1: Yes, with respect to the Earth as reference point its position does not change
strings.b-41.options.2: Yes, because Earth does not move
strings.b-41.options.3: No, because displacement is always zero on Earth
strings.b-41.explanation: Rest and motion depend on the reference point. With respect to Earth the object is at rest, even though Earth moves around the Sun.
strings.b-42.question: Two objects have the same initial and final positions over 10 s on position-time graphs. What can you say about their average velocity over 10 s?
strings.b-42.options.0: Average velocities are equal because displacement and time are equal
strings.b-42.options.2: Average velocity of the curved graph is always higher
strings.b-42.explanation: Average velocity = displacement / time. Same initial and final positions give same displacement, and time is the same, so average velocities are equal. Average speed depends on total distance, which may differ.

lesson.title: Describing Motion Around Us
objectives: After this lesson you can describe position, distance and displacement of an object moving in a straight line.
After this lesson you can calculate average speed, average velocity and average acceleration and use graphs to find them.
After this lesson you can use the kinematic equations for constant acceleration and explain uniform circular motion.

sections.title: Describing position in a straight line
paragraphs: Look around you. Butterflies fly, snakes move, cars run and clouds gather. All of these are in motion. To study motion simply, we first study motion in a straight line. This is called linear motion.

To describe where an object is, we choose a fixed point called the reference point. We then state the distance and the direction of the object from that point. This tells us the position of the object at that instant.
If the position changes with time, the object is in motion. If the position does not change with time, the object is at rest. On a straight line we use plus and minus signs for the two directions.

sections.title: Distance travelled and displacement
paragraphs: Imagine an athlete who runs forward and then runs back on the same track. The total distance travelled is the full length of the path. It is found by adding every part of the journey.

Displacement is different. It is the net change in position between two instants. It needs both a magnitude and a direction. Its magnitude is the straight distance between the starting and finishing positions.

A quantity that needs only a number is called a scalar. A quantity that needs a number and a direction is called a vector. Distance is a scalar and displacement is a vector. The SI unit for both is the metre.

sections.title: Average speed and average velocity
paragraphs: Average speed tells us how fast an object moves. It is total distance travelled divided by the time interval. It has no direction.
If an object travels equal distances in equal intervals of time, it is in uniform motion at constant speed. If the distances are unequal, it is in non-uniform motion.

Average velocity tells us how fast the position changes and in which direction. It is displacement divided by the time interval. Its direction is the same as displacement. Its SI unit is metre per second.

sections.title: Average acceleration
paragraphs: When a vehicle starts suddenly or stops suddenly, you feel a jolt. This is because velocity changes. Average acceleration is change in velocity divided by the time interval.
If the magnitude of velocity increases, acceleration is in the direction of velocity. If the magnitude decreases, acceleration is opposite to velocity. The SI unit is metre per second squared.
An object can move very fast and still have zero acceleration if its velocity is constant. Acceleration depends on how quickly velocity changes, not on speed alone.

sections.title: Position-time graphs
paragraphs: A graph shows how one quantity changes with time. For a position-time graph, time is on the X-axis and position is on the Y-axis. We choose a scale and plot each point carefully.
A straight line position-time graph means constant velocity. A curved graph means velocity is changing and the motion is accelerated. A line parallel to the time axis means the object is at rest.
The slope of a position-time graph gives velocity. Slope is change in position divided by change in time. A steeper line means a higher velocity.

sections.title: Velocity-time graphs
paragraphs: A velocity-time graph shows how velocity changes with time. A line parallel to the X-axis means constant velocity and zero acceleration. A rising straight line means constant acceleration in the direction of velocity.
A falling straight line means constant acceleration opposite to velocity. The slope of a velocity-time graph gives acceleration. Slope is change in velocity divided by change in time.
The area between the graph and the time axis gives displacement. For constant velocity, area is velocity multiplied by time. For changing velocity, we find the area of the shape under the line.

sections.title: Kinematic equations
paragraphs: These equations are used only when acceleration is constant. They connect displacement s, time t, initial velocity u, final velocity v and acceleration a.
The three equations are v = u + at, s = ut + 1/2 at^2 and v^2 = u^2 + 2as. We choose the equation that contains the quantities we know and the quantity we need.
Signs matter. In motion in both directions, the sign of u, v, a and s tells us the direction. When braking, acceleration is negative if velocity is taken as positive.

sections.title: Motion in a plane and uniform circular motion
paragraphs: Motion in a plane is motion in two dimensions. Examples are a kicked ball, a satellite and a vehicle overtaking another. Circular motion is motion along a circular path.
In uniform circular motion the speed is constant but the direction of velocity keeps changing. Velocity at each point is along the tangent to the circle in the direction of motion.

Because direction changes, uniform circular motion is accelerated motion. One revolution has distance equal to the circumference and displacement zero. This is an idealised model that helps us understand real circular motions.

glossary.definition: Net change in position between two instants, with magnitude and direction.
Displacement divided by the time interval.
Change in velocity divided by the time interval.
Steepness of a graph line, giving a rate of change.
Motion in a circle at constant speed with changing velocity direction.
A line touching a circle at only one point.

paragraphs: Everything around us is in motion, from butterflies and horses to clouds and tides. To study this variety simply, scientists first study idealised forms such as linear motion.
Linear motion is motion in a straight line. It is the simplest kind of motion. Examples are a ball falling vertically, a car on a straight highway and a train on a straight track.

steps.detail: He returns to the start, so displacement = 0 m.

spec.answer: Average speed 1 m s-1, average velocity 0 m s-1.

spec.question: You drive 200 km north in three hours, then 200 km south in two hours. What is the average speed for the entire trip?
spec.explanation: Total distance = 400 km. Total time = 5 h. Average speed = 400 / 5 = 80 km h-1. Displacement is zero, so average velocity is zero.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can distinguish average speed from average velocity for a return journey.

paragraphs: Average acceleration is change in velocity divided by the time interval. It is (v - u) / (t2 - t1) with SI unit m s-2.
If magnitude of velocity increases, acceleration is in the direction of velocity. If magnitude decreases, acceleration is opposite to velocity.
Acceleration can come from change in magnitude, change in direction, or both.

spec.problem: A bus moves with velocity 36 km h-1. The driver presses the accelerator for 10 s and velocity increases to 54 km h-1. Then the bus stops in 5 s when brakes are pressed. Find average acceleration in both intervals.

steps.title: Accelerator interval
steps.detail: a = (15 - 10) / 10 = 0.5 m s-2 in the direction of velocity.

steps.title: Brake interval
steps.detail: a = (0 - 15) / 5 = -3 m s-2. Minus sign means opposite to velocity.

spec.answer: (i) 0.5 m s-2 in direction of velocity. (ii) -3 m s-2 opposite to velocity.

spec.problem: An object dropped from a height has velocities 0 m s-1 at 0 s, 9.8 m s-1 at 1 s, 19.6 m s-1 at 2 s, 29.4 m s-1 at 3 s and 39.2 m s-1 at 4 s. Find average acceleration in each 1 s interval.

steps.title: 1 s to 2 s, 2 s to 3 s, 3 s to 4 s
Conclusion
steps.detail: Acceleration is constant at 9.8 m s-2 in the direction of motion. This is g, acceleration due to gravity.

spec.answer: Constant average acceleration 9.8 m s-2 in direction of motion.

spec.question: A scooter speedometer reading is constant. Can the scooter still be accelerating?
options: No, constant speed means no acceleration
Yes, if direction of velocity changes
Yes, if it is moving fast
No, acceleration needs a change in speed only
spec.explanation: Acceleration occurs when velocity changes in magnitude or direction or both. In circular motion speed is constant but direction changes, so acceleration is non-zero.
spec.expected_understanding: Student knows acceleration is not only change in speed.

paragraphs: Graphs show how position, velocity or acceleration changes with time. They help compare motions and find quantities.
To plot, draw X and Y axes from origin O, choose time on X-axis and position on Y-axis, choose a suitable scale, mark points and join them.

steps.title: Draw axes
steps.detail: Draw perpendicular lines OX and OY meeting at origin O on graph paper.

steps.title: Choose scale
steps.detail: For Table 4.3 use X-axis 5 divisions = 1 s and Y-axis 5 divisions = 20 m.

steps.title: Mark points
steps.detail: At 0 s position 0 m is origin. At 1 s position 20 m, at 2 s 40 m, and so on up to 6 s 120 m.

steps.title: Join points
steps.detail: Joining the points gives a straight line for constant velocity data.

spec.problem: For a vehicle starting from rest and speeding up, positions are 0 m at 0 s, 1 m at 2 s, 4 m at 4 s, 9 m at 6 s, 16 m at 8 s, 25 m at 10 s and 36 m at 12 s. Plot the position-time graph.

steps.title: Choose scale
steps.detail: X-axis 5 divisions = 2 s, Y-axis 5 divisions = 5 m.

steps.title: Mark points
steps.detail: Mark each time-position pair from the table.

steps.title: Join points
steps.detail: Points do not fall on a straight line. Join by a curve.

spec.answer: The graph is a curve, showing velocity is increasing.

spec.title: Position-time graph and velocity
spec.description: A position-time graph is drawn from the equation position = velocity x time for constant velocity. Changing the velocity changes the steepness of the line.
spec.learning_goal: See that slope of a position-time graph is velocity and a straight line means constant velocity.
spec.default_behaviour: Shows a straight position-time line for 20 m/s, reaching 120 m at 6 s.

paragraphs: A straight line position-time graph means constant velocity. A curved graph means velocity is not constant.
A line parallel to the time axis means position is not changing, so the object is at rest. A steeper line means higher velocity.

spec.problem: A position-time graph shows a vehicle at 40 m from the origin and position not changing with time. What does it indicate?

steps.title: Read position
steps.detail: Position stays at 40 m for all times.

steps.title: Interpret line
steps.detail: Line is parallel to time axis.

spec.answer: The vehicle is at rest at 40 m from the origin.

spec.problem: Position-time graphs of two objects A and B are given. Which object has higher magnitude of average velocity?

steps.title: Compare displacement in same time
steps.detail: Draw lines parallel to axes for the same time interval.

steps.title: Compare slopes
steps.detail: Displacement of B is more than A in the same time, so slope of B is steeper.

spec.answer: Velocity of B is higher than velocity of A.

steps.title: Take part AB of graph
steps.detail: Draw lines parallel to axes from A and B to form triangle ABC.

steps.title: Identify sides
steps.detail: BC is change in position s2 - s1. CA is change in time t2 - t1.

steps.title: Divide
steps.detail: Velocity = BC / CA = (s2 - s1)/(t2 - t1). Example (80 - 40)/(4 - 2) = 20 m s-1.

paragraphs: A velocity-time graph shows change in velocity with time. Constant velocity gives a line parallel to X-axis and zero acceleration.
Increasing velocity with a straight line gives constant acceleration in the direction of velocity. Decreasing velocity gives constant acceleration opposite to velocity.

spec.title: Velocity-time graph slope and area
spec.description: A velocity-time graph is computed from initial velocity and constant acceleration. Slope gives acceleration and area under the line gives displacement.
spec.learning_goal: Use slope to find acceleration and area to find displacement from a velocity-time graph.
spec.default_behaviour: Shows velocity rising from 0 to 15 m/s in 30 s with slope 0.5 m/s2.

spec.title: Slope and area from velocity-time graph

steps.title: Slope for acceleration
steps.detail: Acceleration = change in velocity / change in time. Between 10 s and 20 s, (10 - 5)/10 = 0.5 m s-2. For decreasing graph it is -0.5 m s-2.

steps.title: Area for displacement, constant velocity
steps.detail: Area of rectangle = velocity x time. 20 m s-1 x 6 s = 120 m.

steps.title: Area for displacement, changing velocity
steps.detail: Between 10 s and 20 s area = rectangle + triangle = 50 m + 25 m = 75 m.

paragraphs: Kinematic equations describe motion with constant acceleration. Acceleration at each instant equals average acceleration.
The five quantities are displacement s, time t, initial velocity u, final velocity v and acceleration a. Choose the equation that fits the known quantities.

steps.title: Velocity equation
steps.detail: From a = (v - u)/t we get at = v - u, so v = u + at.

steps.title: Displacement equation
steps.detail: Displacement is area under velocity-time graph: rectangle + triangle gives s = ut + 1/2 at^2.

steps.title: Velocity squared equation
steps.detail: Eliminate t between the two equations to get v^2 = u^2 + 2as.

spec.problem: A car brakes with acceleration -4 m s-2. How much distance before stopping if it was moving at (i) 54 km h-1 and (ii) 108 km h-1?

steps.title: Convert velocities
steps.detail: (i) 54 km h-1 = 15 m s-1. (ii) 108 km h-1 = 30 m s-1. Final velocity v = 0.

spec.answer: (i) 28.1 m (ii) 112.5 m. Higher initial speed needs much larger stopping distance.

spec.question: Which pair are the remaining two kinematic equations derived from v = u + at and s = ut + 1/2 at^2?
options: s = vt - 1/2 at^2 and s = (u + v)/2 t
v = u - at and s = ut - at^2
s = vt + 1/2 at^2 and v^2 = u^2 - 2as
a = (u - v)/t and s = (u - v) t
spec.explanation: The second equation comes from area of a trapezium under the velocity-time graph, giving s = (u + v)/2 t. The first follows by substitution.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can state and derive the remaining kinematic equations.

paragraphs: Motion in a plane is motion in two dimensions. Examples are a kicked ball, a satellite and a vehicle overtaking another.
Uniform circular motion is motion in a circular path with constant speed. One revolution distance is the circumference, displacement is zero, average speed is 2 pi R / T and average velocity is zero.

spec.caption: Circular path A to B to C. Velocity at B is along the tangent in the direction of motion.

spec.title: Uniform circular motion
spec.description: A point moves on a circle at constant speed. Its velocity arrow is always along the tangent and changes direction continuously.
spec.learning_goal: See that speed is constant but velocity direction changes, so motion is accelerated.
spec.default_behaviour: Shows a point moving round a circle with a tangent velocity arrow, completing one revolution in 10 s.

paragraphs: Velocity at a point is along the tangent to the circle in the direction of motion. A tangent meets the circle at only one point.
When a marble moving inside a ring is released, it moves in a straight line in the direction at the instant of release.
Uniform circular motion is an idealised model. It is useful for planets around the Sun and vehicles making circular turns.

spec.question: A man goes from home to a shop 250 m away, returns home, goes to the shop again and returns home. What are total distance and displacement from home?
spec.explanation: Four journeys of 250 m give total distance 1000 m. He ends at home, so net change in position is zero.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can calculate total distance and displacement for back-and-forth motion.

spec.question: A car starts from rest and its velocity reaches 24 m s-1 in 6 s. Find average acceleration and distance travelled in 6 s.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can use average acceleration and kinematic equations from rest.

spec.question: A motorbike moving with initial velocity 28 m s-1 and constant acceleration stops after travelling 98 m. Find acceleration and time to stop.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can use v^2 = u^2 + 2as and v = u + at for stopping motion.

spec.question: A truck at 54 km h-1 slows to 36 km h-1 in 36 s with constant acceleration. What distance does it travel?
spec.explanation: Convert to 15 m s-1 and 10 m s-1. Average velocity = 12.5 m s-1. Distance = 12.5 x 36 = 450 m.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can convert units and use average velocity for distance.

spec.question: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 20 m s-1 in 5 s, travels at 20 m s-1 for 10 s, then brakes uniformly to stop in 6 s. Find total distance.
spec.explanation: Phase 1: a = 4 m s-2, s = 50 m. Phase 2: s = 200 m. Phase 3: a = -3.33 m s-2, s = 60 m. Total = 310 m.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can combine three stages of motion with constant acceleration.

spec.question: On a velocity-time graph, what does the area between the graph and the time axis represent?
spec.explanation: Area = velocity x time for constant velocity and area of the shape for changing velocity. Both give displacement in that time interval.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can read displacement from area under a velocity-time graph.

spec.question: The Earth moves around the Sun. Can an object kept on the Earth be considered at rest?
options: No, nothing on Earth can ever be at rest
Yes, with respect to the Earth as reference point its position does not change
Yes, because Earth does not move
No, because displacement is always zero on Earth
spec.explanation: Rest and motion depend on the reference point. With respect to Earth the object is at rest, even though Earth moves around the Sun.
spec.expected_understanding: Student understands rest is relative to a reference point.

spec.question: Two objects have the same initial and final positions over 10 s on position-time graphs. What can you say about their average velocity over 10 s?
options: Average velocities are equal because displacement and time are equal
Average velocity of the curved graph is always higher
spec.explanation: Average velocity = displacement / time. Same initial and final positions give same displacement, and time is the same, so average velocities are equal. Average speed depends on total distance, which may differ.
spec.expected_understanding: Student can use slope and displacement ideas to compare average velocity and average speed from position-time graphs.
